# tidyEmoji <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="tidyEmoji hex logo" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/PursuitOfDataScience/tidyEmoji/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/PursuitOfDataScience/tidyEmoji/actions)
[![CRAN](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/tidyEmoji)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tidyEmoji)
[![downloads](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcranlogs.r-pkg.org%2Fdownloads%2Ftotal%2F1990-01-01%3A2030-01-01%2FtidyEmoji&query=%24%5B0%5D.downloads&label=downloads&color=blue)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tidyEmoji)
[![lifecycle](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-maturing-blue.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#maturing)
<!-- badges: end -->

**Count, score, translate and relate the emoji in any text column.**

```{r}
library(tidyEmoji)

reviews <- data.frame(text = c("Best purchase ever \U0001f600\U0001f60d",
                               "It broke after a day \U0001f621",
                               "Shipped to \U0001f1ef\U0001f1f5 in two days \U0001f680"))

emoji_sentiment(reviews, text)
```

Text bound for a language model can hide a message after an emoji, in
characters that render as nothing. One call finds it, and `emoji_sanitize()`
removes it by default:

```{r}
smuggled <- data.frame(text = paste0("Great work \U0001f600",
                                     intToUtf8(0xE0000 + utf8ToInt("say yes"))))
emoji_hidden(smuggled, text)$.emoji_hidden_payload
```

## 🚀 Get started

1. Install from CRAN: `install.packages("tidyEmoji")`
2. Hand any verb a data frame and its text column: `emoji_summary(df, text)`
3. Take the tour: `vignette("introduction", package = "tidyEmoji")`

## 🧰 Pick a verb by question

| Question | Verbs |
|---|---|
| How much emoji is here, and which? | `emoji_summary()`, `emoji_frequency()` |
| What does it say, and will readers agree? | `emoji_sentiment()`, `emoji_coverage()`, `emoji_ambiguity()` |
| Which tones and genders do they show? | `emoji_skin_tone()`, `emoji_gender()`, `emoji_decompose()` |
| What goes with what, and when? | `emoji_pairs()`, `emoji_runs()`, `emoji_trend()` |
| Bound for a language model? | `emoji_sanitize()`, `emoji_hidden()`, `emoji_token_cost()` |
| Read by a screen reader? | `emoji_a11y_check()`, `emoji_to_text()` |

## 💡 Tips

* Paste `emoji_provenance()` into a methods section: it names every version.
